title.purpose: Big buttons (Play hand, Discard, Play, Start run, Resume), the Shop's Next Blind, the cash-out total and the plaque's hand name, uppercase; sheet names, a pack's reading-plate name, the run setup's Deck name and How to play's page titles in their own case at .02em; at the table layout price tags and the payout's hanging tags and note pops too. 30 px while the art pixel is 3 CSS px. Collect $N is a regular button, set as Tag.

title-compact.purpose: The same roles at 20 px, Jersey 10's own 2x grid, once the art pixel is 2 CSS px; the cash-out total stays 30 px in the compact layout.

tag.purpose: Pills, regular buttons (Collect $N among them), tabs and Boss names, uppercase at .03em; Tag, Shop item and tooltip names in their own case at .02em; section heads in Overview, Options and the run setup uppercase at .04 to .08em.

label.purpose: Small labels (Hands, Discards, Money, Ante), Joker and consumable plates, small buttons, tooltip kinds; Tiny5's own 16 px grid everywhere, phone plates included.

copy.purpose: Descriptions, tooltips, sheets, How to play and toasts, with bold keywords in their system colour.

copy-small.purpose: Boss rules, Tag texts, the sheet's why line, Shop item texts, Options hints, Overview's details and the notes on the menus and end screens (line-height 1.25 to 1.32 in the tighter Shop, Blind select and Records texts). Never smaller.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.value: 0 calc(4 * var(--px)) calc(9 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.46), 0 var(--px) var(--px) rgba(26,4,18,.42)
shadows.purpose: Every 9-slice panel, drawn on its own ::before plate so a panel can pulse without its shadow jumping; it also draws the bottom edge.

shadows.name: button
shadows.value: 0 calc(3 * var(--px)) calc(8 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.45), 0 var(--px) calc(2 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.3)
shadows.purpose: Pressable buttons; the plate fades to .35 opacity when the button is disabled.

shadows.name: pill
shadows.purpose: Every pill, on a plate inset 1 by 2 art px.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.value: 0 calc(7 * var(--px)) calc(20 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.65), 0 var(--px) calc(2 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.45)
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and the cash-out, over a rgba(26,4,18,.55) scrim with a warm pool of light behind.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.value: 0 calc(6 * var(--px)) calc(16 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.62), 0 var(--px) calc(2 * var(--px)) rgba(26,4,18,.45)
shadows.purpose: Item sheets anchored to their item, and bottom sheets in the compact layout.

shadows.name: card-contact-ambient
shadows.value: radial-gradient ellipses in rgba(26,4,18,a) under the card (no blur filters)
shadows.purpose: A tight dark ellipse under each card and a wide soft radial below it, drawn on the table; they stay behind when the card lifts.

shadows.name: chosen-card
shadows.value: 1 art px rim #FFDDB0 + ember halo; translateY(calc(-10 * var(--px)))
shadows.purpose: A chosen card: a peach rim and an ember halo round the face; it rises 10 art px (14 in the compact layout, and 10 again on every compact window 760 px tall or less: a short upright phone, a compact window held upright, a landscape phone, a short window held wide).

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The two-tone keyboard focus ring: pale yellow outside, a band of the ink edge inside, for keyboard users only.

shadows.name: glow-chips
shadows.purpose: Live Chips numerals: a tight core plus a blue halo.

shadows.name: glow-mult
shadows.purpose: Live Mult numerals: a tight core plus a red halo.

shadows.name: glow-money
shadows.purpose: Money keeps only its core, no halo.

shadows.name: glow-vio
shadows.purpose: Violet readouts and marks (consumables, the Boss).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrances, presses, hover filters and the route change's fade.

motion.name: spring
motion.value: damped spring, zeta 0.62, sampled into linear() (fallback cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.4, 0.64, 1), one source in 00-core.js for the CSS and the Web Animations)
motion.purpose: Lifts, deals, sorts, entrances and dialogs springing in; a chosen fanned card's Seal glides on it too.

motion.name: spring-soft
motion.value: damped spring, zeta 0.86, sampled into linear() (fallback cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), from the same source)
motion.purpose: The room's parallax lean, following a fine pointer over 1400 ms at the Relaxed pace.

motion.name: spring-bouncy
motion.value: damped spring, zeta 0.42, sampled into linear() (fallback cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.7, 0.64, 1), from the same source)
motion.purpose: The plaque's drop and swell, the payout's pixel shards, number and note pops, hanging tags and the spring back of every punch.

motion.name: t-press
motion.purpose: A button's press (Relaxed pace; every --t-* is divided by the game speed).

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Hover filters, the switch knob, a tab label's colour.

motion.name: t-lift
motion.purpose: A card's lift and its Seal's glide.

motion.name: route-fade
motion.value: 180ms (whole view), 160ms (the table's main area); ease-out; not divided by the game speed
motion.purpose: A lifeless copy of the leaving view, its cards' wash, sweep and Edition light left out, fades out in place, under reduced motion too; the main area's copy is fixed over its area and the whole view's lies out of flow at the top of the page, so neither joins the page's flow. A new visit to the Shop builds its shelves a task later, once the screen change has had its frame, with input held.

motion.name: game-speed
motion.purpose: Divides every gameplay duration; ambient loops keep their own pace; test mode zeroes every duration.

motion.name: ambient-loops
motion.value: room drift 46s and 31s; hearth 7.5s; pool 9s; flame 0.9s in three steps; bloom 2.6s
motion.purpose: The room's life, at its own pace; held still under reduced motion and in test mode.

motion.name: edition-light
motion.value: Glitch slices 3.4s step-end; Sheen 3.2s in 24 steps; Dither 2.4s in 4 steps; Phantom 2.4s steps(1)
motion.purpose: Edition light in whole art pixels, never rotating: ambient, not divided by the game speed, held still under reduced motion.

breakpoints.name: art-px-2
breakpoints.purpose: The art pixel drops from 3 to 2 CSS px, and button and title type from 30 to 20 px (TW.UI.MQ.px2).

breakpoints.name: table
breakpoints.purpose: The table layout's own rules: a run's toasts over the field under the racks, Night Market's two rows on one grid of four, a pack's stage one field wide.

breakpoints.name: narrow-3px-table
breakpoints.purpose: A pack of six scrolls its row inside the field where it doesn't fit (a thin scrollbar, no snap); beside a dealt hand the reading plate is 70 by 100 art px and the deck steps aside (44 px strips at 1024 px); Play hand and Discard keep their label's width; the Shop's shelves hold two items a row, scrolling inside the panel when they are taller than it.

breakpoints.name: short-laptop
breakpoints.purpose: The table layout at art pixel 2; beside a dealt hand the reading plate is 120 by 104 art px.

breakpoints.name: short-laptop-shop
breakpoints.purpose: The Shop's item text keeps three lines: at 820 px tall or less with Night Market, at 760 or less without.

breakpoints.name: short-laptop-700
breakpoints.purpose: Two lines of Shop text, the kind line stepping aside and the shelves closer; a Boss's name leaves its rule, the column's panels sit 5 art px apart, the Blind score's panel is 40 art px and the wells 32, so Overview and Options stay above the fold.

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.purpose: The column becomes a top bar (a status column on a landscape phone), the Joker rack scrolls sideways with snap and sheets rise from the bottom; touch targets 44 px; a run's toasts sit 30 art px over the foot (118 down over a pack), a menu's or end screen's at the top.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: A two-row top bar; the hand keeps the table's measure, centred; a Shop item stands art beside its text (on a window 870 px tall or more), and the reading plate over a dealt hand is 52 art px.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: A three-row top bar and an edge-to-edge fanned hand.

breakpoints.name: short-phone
breakpoints.purpose: A tighter bar, 40 px strips at 360 x 640, a chosen card rising 10 art px, one-screen Shop and packs, the racks aside for a dealt hand.

breakpoints.name: short-phone-blinds
breakpoints.purpose: The Blind select's candles and Boss emblem step aside, so the three Blinds fit under the racks.

breakpoints.name: compact-short
breakpoints.purpose: A shorter stage and Blind emblems.

breakpoints.name: upright-window
breakpoints.purpose: The top bar's two rows set out again: the Blind (half the bar, a Boss rule in two lines), the Blind score and money; Chips x Mult beside the counts and buttons; Ante and the Blind count step aside on the table.

breakpoints.name: short-upright-window
breakpoints.value: (min-width: 600px) and (max-width: 1023px) and (max-height: 760px) and (orientation: portrait), with (max-height: 619px) inside
breakpoints.purpose: The stage gives up its room and a chosen card rises 10 art px; at the Blind select the candles and Boss emblem step aside, and a Boss rule leaves the bar for up to four lines on its Blind, three under 620 px tall.

breakpoints.name: wide-short-compact
breakpoints.purpose: The racks step aside for a pack's dealt hand and, on a window held upright, for a Planet Pack too; a short window held wide brings them back for every pack (its own query).

breakpoints.name: short-compact-shop
breakpoints.value: (min-width: 600px) and (max-width: 1023px) and (max-height: 869px), not a landscape phone
breakpoints.purpose: The Shop's items in one row under its head, each as on a phone held upright, sharing their shelf's rows so every Buy stands at one height, the reason under Buy in up to three lines; Night Market's seven scroll sideways where they don't fit.

breakpoints.name: landscape
breakpoints.purpose: A narrow status column at the left, the buttons in a column beside the hand, the two-column pack with its dealt hand: a landscape phone, and a short window held wide.

breakpoints.name: landscape-phone
breakpoints.purpose: What stays a phone's: the waiting Tags strip steps aside (as on a short upright phone), and the Shop keeps its head column beside one row of items.

breakpoints.name: short-wide-window
breakpoints.purpose: The landscape layout with the table's column given back (candle, whole Boss rule, money beside Ante and the Blind count, Overview and Options named at its foot), the Blind select's candles and waiting Tags, the racks kept over every pack, a pack with no dealt hand set out as in the compact layout (its head in a row, its cards across the field, the reading plate under them), the one-row Shop, and toasts under the racks.

breakpoints.name: menus-stack
breakpoints.purpose: The title, setup and Overview plates stack.

breakpoints.name: menus-one-column
breakpoints.purpose: The menus take one column, their big buttons 24 art px tall.

breakpoints.name: short-setup
breakpoints.purpose: The run setup's plate is the window's height and its Deck and Stake scroll inside it, so the stats, Back and Start run stay in view.

breakpoints.name: short-end-screens
breakpoints.purpose: The end screens draw their rows in, so Game Over and You win! fit whole on a window from 600 px wide and 600 px tall; from 600 to 760 px wide their counts stand three a row.

breakpoints.name: fine-pointer
breakpoints.purpose: Hover states (button brightness, card lift) only where a pointer hovers.

narrative.overview:
Wickwager is a poker-hand roguelike played at a card table in a warm room lit by candles. The approved Ember pixel table is relit as a 2026 indie game: crisp pixel sprites sit at one whole-number scale, and light, bloom, glow, shadow and depth are separate layers around them, never baked into a smoothed sprite. The room has three depths behind every screen: a far wall of irregular candle groups out of focus, a middle layer of pixel haze, and embers rising near the glass. A hearth glow rises from below, a pool of candlelight sits over the stage, and the edges fall away into warm plum, never black.

Density is a game table's: every number the player needs (Target, Blind score, Chips × Mult, hands, discards, money) sits on screen in its own lit panel, each number glowing in its own colour. Chrome is soft pixel 9-slice panels with a two-pixel warm lip along the top, pills for labels, and buttons whose lip sinks when pressed. Things that land move on damped springs; the scoring moment, the payout, is the reward and ends in a plaque, rings, pixel shards and a flash of the room.

The owner rejected three earlier looks, and their reasons stand as rules: the parchment logbook; the navy-and-gold pier arcade (it felt like a phone casino app, was too dark and all one colour, its cards looked plain, and scoring wasn't juicy enough); and comic pop, along with the cooler "Night" pixel look. The game follows the genre's design and system words, and its look is its own.
keyCharacteristics: One art-pixel size per screen (--px is 3 or 2 CSS px), image-rendering: pixelated, nothing rotated at rest.
A warm plum-to-burnt-orange room in seven bands, with light as additive layers (plus-lighter).
Every colour has a job: blue Chips, red Mult, flat yellow money, ember for the main action, pink for Discard and Jokers, lime for the Blind score, violet for consumables and the Boss.
Three type faces with strict roles, plus the Ember digit face (a bitmap drawn in code) for every readout.
Every shadow is tinted plum (rgb(26 4 18)), never grey or black.
Damped springs sampled into linear(); one game speed divides every gameplay duration.

rules.name: The One Job Rule
rules.body: Each accent means one thing. Blue is always Chips, red always Mult, yellow always money, ember always the way forward. The shipped exceptions are few and fixed: a pressed toggle segment sinks in yellow and the focus ring's outer colour is pale yellow; Planet cards share the Chips blue; ember also marks the Hands count, a chosen tab's bar, a slider's fill and a chosen card's halo. A new screen never borrows an accent for decoration.

rules.name: The Flat Cash Rule
rules.body: Money is flat yellow with one amber rim. No gold ramp, no chrome trim, no coins, bulbs or jackpot banners on a money figure. In the art the gold ramp is ornament (crowns, bells, buttons, buckles, chains, gilt edges, sequins, a sun or a star), never coded as money, and the few coins drawn into items (Busker's Hat, Cursed Coin, the Rags to Riches Deck's sewn-on coin) are flat yellow with one amber rim as well.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow, scrim and vignette is the plum tint rgb(26 4 18) at some alpha; only the inset rims of the small wells (the seed field and its readout, a slider's track) take a deeper plum, rgb(10 2 8). Nothing is grey, nothing is black.

rules.name: The Whole Grid Rule
rules.body: A pixel face is set only at a whole multiple of its own grid: Jersey 10 at 20 or 30 px, Tiny5 at 16 px. The button and title size drops from 30 to 20 px together with --px. The shipped exceptions set Jersey 10 at 16 px, off its grid: the compact Blind select's pills and Boss and Tag names, the waiting Tags' names in the compact layout, a phone title's four menu buttons, and a Joker's Off and +1 marks.

rules.name: The Fifteen Pixel Floor
rules.body: Long copy is Bricolage Grotesque at 15 px or more. Pixel faces never set a paragraph; Bricolage never sets a pill, a button, a small label or a readout (a number inside its sentences, such as +4 Mult, stays in the sentence's face).

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Never two art-pixel sizes on one screen at rest (a press, a pulse, a swell or the total's flight scales a sprite only while it moves), and no sprite rests between pixels except in the cases The art pixel names; the room's drifting layers glide freely. The one exception to the breakpoint's scale is the reference sheet (gallery.html), which shows every sprite at the one whole scale its page asks for (3 by default; 2 and 6 on its links).

rules.name: The Redraw In Place Rule
rules.body: Crossing a breakpoint (a window crossing 1024 px wide or 870 px tall, a phone turned) redraws only what was drawn for one pixel size: the name plates, lettering and pools of light on the menus and in an open dialog, the table's column and racks, the Shop or an open pack, and the room. Focus stays on the same control or the one drawn in its place, an open dialog stays open, and a redraw asked for while the game is busy waits for it instead of being dropped. Any resize, one that crosses no breakpoint too, fits the column's figures (the target, the Blind score, money) to their panels again, though never while a payout runs or input is held.

rules.name: The Light Layer Rule
rules.body: Light, glow, bloom and shadow are separate CSS layers or small stretched canvases around the sprites. A sprite's pixels are never blurred, smoothed or filtered for depth; the far room and the far and near embers are the only blurred art, by design.

dos: Do size every sprite, gap and resting offset in whole art pixels (calc(n * var(--px))), with --px 3 at 1024 × 870 and up and 2 below either.
Do give each accent its one job: Chips #4A62FF, Mult #E9382B, money #FFCE3B flat with a #D18A1D rim, ember #FF7A2B for the way forward.
Do tint every shadow, scrim and vignette plum (rgb(26 4 18)).
Do set labels in Jersey 10 (20/30 px) or Tiny5 (16 px), readouts in the Ember digit face, and sentences in Bricolage Grotesque at 15 px or more with coloured keywords.

Do animate only transform, opacity and filter, with CSS transitions, CSS animations or WAAPI (the shipped exceptions: the candle flames and Dither's dots step their background-position, a tab label's hover colour eases over 160 ms, and a chosen fanned card's Seal glides its top with the lift); land things on the damped springs (spring zeta 0.62, soft 0.86, bouncy 0.42, sampled into linear()) and enter on cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1).

Do divide every gameplay duration by the game speed (Relaxed 1, Normal 1.6 (default), Fast 2.6, Blazing 4.5); keep ambient loops (room drift 46 s and 31 s, hearth 7.5 s, pool 9 s, flame 0.9 s in three steps, bloom 2.6 s, Edition light) at their own pace; zero every duration in test mode.
Do keep fades only under reduced motion (the system setting or Options): no shake, flash, drift, parallax, glint, sweep, shard or flicker, and numbers land at once.

Do pair each payout beat with its sound: select, deselect, deal, play, chip, mult, xmult, again (Encore!), total, beaten, collect, money, discard, boss, tag, buy, sell, reroll, pack, pick, use, skip, shuffle, flip, button, error, lose, win; all synthesised in the key of D major (the Game Over line borrows D minor's F, the Boss Blind's gong a G-sharp tritone), scoring ticks climbing the D major pentatonic, panned to where the source sits.

Do show focus as the two-tone ring (2 px #FFF0A0 outside, an #2B1220 band inside, 3 px gap) for keyboard users only; bring a focused card above its neighbours; return focus to the opener (or the control drawn in its place) when a dialog closes, without opening its tip; leave room for the ring inside everything that scrolls (6 px in most: a dialog body, the compact Joker rack, the Shop's shelves and rows, a pack's options, the run setup's Deck and Stake) so no ring is cut, and scroll a control the keyboard focuses there whole into view.
Do keep every control a real button whose name starts with the word it shows, and the table playable from the keyboard (1 to 9, Enter, D, S, I, Esc; Shift with an arrow moves a card).
Do keep text at 4.5:1 against the pixels actually behind it, large numerals at 3:1; step a pill one shade deeper or put a plum pool under a label rather than fade it.
donts: Don't lay a filter over the screen, give text a hard drop shadow, or borrow another game's look: the room, the type, the panels and the colours are this file's (Overview, Colors, Typography, Components).

Don't copy another game's card, Joker, deck-back or stake art, or its logo, item names, text or menu copy, and never give an item the same effect and the same number as one on the off-limits list (SPEC.md §0).
Don't draw a Seal as a wax blob or a round disc: the four Seals are the shapes of Editions and Seals, and none is gold.
Don't give an Edition any look but its own (Editions and Seals: Glitch's fringe, Sheen's sweep, Dither's dots, Phantom's pale ghost), and let the score glow, never burn.
Don't code money in gold: no gold ramps, chrome trims, coins, bulbs, jackpot banners or other casino cues.
Don't set the room's candles in rows or bulb strips: candle groups stay irregular.
Don't go all one colour or dark: the room stays plum to burnt orange and the edges fall into warm plum, never black.
Don't make cards plain, or scoring quiet: the payout stays as juicy as Lit's peak or juicier.
Don't rotate a sprite at rest, smooth or blur sprite pixels, or show two art-pixel sizes on one screen.
Don't set long copy in a pixel face, or any copy below 15 px.
Don't use harlequin diamonds or commedia half-masks, a parchment logbook, or the navy-and-gold pier arcade.
